ateret_zekenim.en: ) One may not kindle in their shells even if they are fit for animal food, etc. It appears to me this is not precise, for we hold like R' Shimon as stated in chapter Nolad (Shabbos 143) — see there, R' Nasan: we have only Beit Hillel like R' Shimon, etc. R' Shimon permits only what is fit for animal food as taught in the mishnah because it is fit for animal food. See Tosafos there and Asheri. Accordingly all poskim follow this. Therefore it appears the Rambam, Tur, and Shulchan Aruch did not bring the law of date pits because some are fit for animal food and some are not as stated in the gemara there. See what was written above siman 459 skh 8 regarding fats fit for dogs — permitted to move if slaughtered on Yom Tov; so too here. What the Shulchan Aruch wrote — that if he ate on Yom Tov one may not kindle in shells — refers to walnuts and almonds whose shells are not fit for animal food; but where shells are fit for animal food it is plainly permitted, not like the Magen Avraham author. What the Rosh wrote at the end of Beitzah is not so, for the Rosh wrote in Peulat as Beit Hillel but per R' Chananel not so; other poskim hold not like R' Chananel and only permit if fit for animal food, as I wrote siman 499 bringing the Rosh in Nolad. I already wrote to distinguish Tosafos in chapter Ma Tovim 29a — reasoning for prohibition on nuts unlike duck feathers which permit goose feathers or date pits because nut shells are not needed for the food; if he intends to kindle with them he should remove from erev Yom Tov unlike duck feathers. Also date pits needed for the food itself cannot be removed erev Yom Tov therefore permitted. (Maharar Tzvi Shpitz)

peri_megadim.he: ולפידים עט״ז אפייה ובישול היינו לצורך היום ונשאר למחר ג״כ ועד״מ וב״ח. ור״ה אף למ״ד ב׳ קדושות בביצה נולדה בזה אסורה בזה ואף למ״ד קדושה א׳ לחומרא ולא לקולא משא״כ י״ט של גליות גם ביצה נולדה בזה מותרת בשני דממ״נ א׳ חול. ועפר״ח דמתיר די״ט לעצמו הכין כבסי׳ תצ״ח. ועמ״א אות י״ו מזה ומ״מ גם הפר״ח כתב המחמיר תע״ב. ועא״ר אות י״ב ובלבוש שכ״ב ותקי״ד ועיין יש״ש ביצה פרק א׳ סימן ג׳ וד׳ משמע דמחמיר בשיורי שמן ופתילה אף בו ביום לחזור ולהדליק יע״ש. ולפ״ז לכאורה ג׳ דנים פתילה י״א כלי הוי ולצורך גופו ומקומו שרי בטלטול עכ״פ וי״א דלא הוי כלי ואסור בטילטול דמצד הב׳ נמי הוי הכנה יע״ש ביש״ש ולפידים כה״ג ודאי לאו כלי ואסור לצורך גופו ומקומו שמן אם ראוי לאכילה י״ל שרי בטילטול לכ״ע ואי״ה במ״א י״ו יבואר עוד:
peri_megadim.en: And torches — roasting and cooking for today's need and remains tomorrow as well. Rosh HaShana — even for two sanctities in Beitzah egg born on one forbidden on other; even one sanctity stringently not leniently unlike diaspora Yom Tov also egg born on one permitted on second since one is chol. Peri Chadash permits Yom Tov for itself as siman 498. Magen Avraham letter 16 from this; nevertheless Peri Chadash wrote to be stringent erev. See letter 12 in Levush 22 and 514; see Yeshuos Yaakov Beitzah chapter 1 simanim 3-4 — implies stringent on leftover oil and wick even same day to relight. Therefore three views on wick: (1) vessel — for body and place permitted at least to move; (2) not vessel forbidden to move — from three also preparation; Yeshuos Yaakov; torches likewise certainly not vessel forbidden for body and place; oil if edible perhaps permitted to move for all — see Magen Avraham 16.
